::: {.lead}
Our investigations are organised into complementary lines, ranging from the
prospection of novel viruses in sequencing data to the experimental validation
of virus–host interaction mechanisms.
:::

<!-- AJUSTAR: revisar titulos, descricoes e palavras-chave de cada linha -->

::: {.research-line}
::: {.research-index}
01
:::
::: {.research-content}
### Discovery and characterisation of novel viruses

Prospection of viral genomes in metagenomic and metatranscriptomic data from
invertebrates, vertebrates, plants and environmental samples, including
assembly, curation, taxonomic classification and formal description of new viral
species.

::: {.tag-list}
- virome
- metagenomics
- viral taxonomy
:::
:::
:::

::: {.research-line}
::: {.research-index}
02
:::
::: {.research-content}
### Comparative genomics and viral evolution

Phylogenetic and comparative genomic analyses to reconstruct the evolutionary
history of viral families, investigate recombination events and map distribution
patterns across hosts.

::: {.tag-list}
- phylogenetics
- recombination
- coevolution
:::
:::
:::

::: {.research-line}
::: {.research-index}
03
:::
::: {.research-content}
### Virus–host interaction and antiviral immunity

Study of host antiviral responses, with emphasis on RNA interference pathways
and other mechanisms controlling viral replication in invertebrates.

::: {.tag-list}
- RNAi
- small RNAs
- innate immunity
:::
:::
:::

::: {.research-line}
::: {.research-index}
04
:::
::: {.research-content}
### Bioinformatics and tool development

Construction of reproducible pipelines and open computational tools for the
detection, annotation and visualisation of viral sequences, focused on usability
and scalability.

::: {.tag-list}
- pipelines
- open source
- reproducibility
:::
:::
:::

::: {.research-line}
::: {.research-index}
05
:::
::: {.research-content}
### Viruses of agricultural and One Health interest

Characterisation of viruses associated with crops, vectors and animals of
economic and sanitary importance, connecting genomic surveillance with the One
Health perspective.

::: {.tag-list}
- plant viruses
- arboviruses
- genomic surveillance
:::
:::
:::
